unit-bee1.title: Spelling Bee · List 1
unit-bee1.srcName: Spelling Bee Words — 2026-27 Scripps 'Two Bee' 4th Grade Study List (Drive)
unit-bee1.source: Scripps National Spelling Bee, 2026-27 Two Bee Study Words for Fourth Grade — official 50-word study list (Drive)

summary.text: List 1 of River's Spelling Bee study words: buttons, tiptoed, cuddle, clever, puffy, basement, burlap, wetlands, invite, butterflies, kelp, property, carefully.

why.text: This is the real Scripps "Two Bee" fourth-grade word list — the words a school spelling bee actually draws from. Saying each word aloud, letter by letter, is the same skill a real bee tests, not just recognizing the word on a page.

objectives.text: Spell every word on this list correctly, letter by letter, from hearing it alone.
State each word's meaning in your own words.

parentNote.text: Built from "Spelling Bee Words", the 2026-27 Scripps Two Bee fourth-grade study list you added to her Drive folder. All 50 official words are split across four lessons; every definition and example sentence here was written fresh, since the source is a bare word list with no definitions to copy. The flashcards use the honeycomb "bee" look, and each lesson also opens the Spelling Bee voice game — hear it, spell it aloud letter by letter.

nextUp.text: Cards first to learn the meanings, then the Spelling Bee game to practice saying the letters aloud.

cards.def:
**Small fastening discs sewn onto clothing that slip through a buttonhole to hold it closed.**
• She counted six buttons down the front of the coat.
cards.hint: Double T — BUT-tons, not one T.

cards.def:
**Walked quietly and carefully on the tips of the toes, to avoid making noise.**
• She tiptoed past the sleeping baby's door.
cards.hint: TIP + TOED — two small words hiding inside the big one.

cards.def:
**To hold someone or something closely and warmly, usually while sitting or lying down.**
• The kitten liked to cuddle up in the blanket.
cards.hint: Double D — CUD-dle, not one D.

cards.def:
**Quick to think of smart ideas or solve problems in an original way.**
• Her clever plan solved the puzzle in half the time.
cards.hint: CLEV-er — one V, like most of "eleven".

cards.def:
**Swollen, rounded, or puffed out — often used for clouds, eyes, or sleeves.**
• Puffy white clouds drifted across the summer sky.

**The floor of a building that sits below ground level.**
• The old trunks were stored in the basement.
cards.hint: BASE + MENT — the base of the building, plus -ment.

cards.def:
**A coarse, rough fabric woven from jute or hemp fibers.**
• The potatoes were shipped to market in a burlap sack.
cards.hint: Two syllables: BUR-lap — the "ur" sounds like "fur", not "ber".

cards.def:
**Low-lying land that is soaked with water for all or part of the year, like a marsh or swamp.**
• Herons and turtles both make their homes in the wetlands.
cards.hint: WET + LANDS — land that stays wet.

cards.def:
**To ask someone to come to an event or to take part in something.**
• They plan to invite the whole class to the party.
cards.hint: IN- + -VITE, like "invitation" with the ending cut off.

cards.def:
**Insects with two pairs of large, often brightly patterned wings, that go through a caterpillar stage first.**
• Orange and black butterflies gathered on the milkweed plant.
cards.hint: BUTTER + FLIES — and FLY changes Y to I before -es.

cards.def:
**A large brown seaweed that grows in cold coastal waters, sometimes forming underwater forests.**
• Sea otters wrap themselves in kelp to keep from drifting out to sea.

**Something that belongs to a person, or the land and buildings someone owns.**
• The old barn is still standing on their property.

**Done with close attention, so as to avoid mistakes, damage, or danger.**
• She carefully carried the stack of glass plates to the sink.
cards.hint: CARE + FUL + LY — double L where "full" meets "ly".

questions.q: Spell the word: small fastening discs sewn onto clothing that slip through a buttonhole to hold it closed.
questions.hint: Double T — BUT-tons, not one T.
steps: The middle doubles the T: B-U-T-T.

ex.tip: A single T would say "BYOO-tons" — the double T keeps the short U sound.

questions.q: Spell the word: walked quietly and carefully on the tips of the toes, to avoid making noise.
questions.hint: TIP + TOED — two small words hiding inside the big one.
steps: Two small words joined: tip and toed.
The "toe" keeps its E before the D.

ex.tip: "Toed" is "toe" plus D for past tense — the E does not drop.

questions.q: Spell the word: to hold someone or something closely and warmly, usually while sitting or lying down.
questions.hint: Double D — CUD-dle, not one D.
steps: The middle doubles the D: C-U-D-D.

ex.tip: One D would make the U sound long, like in "food" — the double D keeps it short.

questions.q: Spell the word: quick to think of smart ideas or solve problems in an original way.
questions.hint: CLEV-er — one V, like most of "eleven".
steps: C-L-E-V — just one V in the middle.

ex.tip: No double letters anywhere in this one — it is shorter than it sounds.

questions.q: Spell the word: swollen, rounded, or puffed out — often used for clouds, eyes, or sleeves.
steps: Swap the silent nothing for a Y at the end.

ex.tip: "Puff" already has the double F — this word just adds a Y.

questions.q: Spell the word: the floor of a building that sits below ground level.
questions.hint: BASE + MENT — the base of the building, plus -ment.

ex.tip: The E in "base" stays even with -ment added after it.

questions.q: Spell the word: a coarse, rough fabric woven from jute or hemp fibers.
questions.hint: Two syllables: BUR-lap — the "ur" sounds like "fur", not "ber".

ex.tip: Say "fur" in your head first — "bur" rhymes with it exactly.

questions.q: Spell the word: low-lying land that is soaked with water for all or part of the year, like a marsh or swamp.
questions.hint: WET + LANDS — land that stays wet.
steps: Two small words: wet and lands.
No joining letters needed — just put them together.

ex.tip: Both halves are words you already know how to spell on their own.

questions.q: Spell the word: to ask someone to come to an event or to take part in something.
questions.hint: IN- + -VITE, like "invitation" with the ending cut off.
steps: The silent E at the end makes the I say its own name.

ex.tip: Without the final E it would read "invit" — the E is what makes it "vite".

questions.q: Spell the word: insects with two pairs of large, often brightly patterned wings, that go through a caterpillar stage first.
questions.hint: BUTTER + FLIES — and FLY changes Y to I before -es.
steps: Two words joined: butter and flies.
"Fly" drops its Y and adds -ies: F-L-I-E-S.

ex.tip: "Fly" alone ends in Y, but the plural swaps that Y for I before -es.

questions.q: Spell the word: a large brown seaweed that grows in cold coastal waters, sometimes forming underwater forests.
steps: Say it once, all the way through.

ex.tip: No silent letters and no tricks — it is spelled exactly how it sounds.

questions.q: Spell the word: something that belongs to a person, or the land and buildings someone owns.

ex.tip: "Prop" only has one P even though the whole word sounds heavy.

questions.q: Spell the word: done with close attention, so as to avoid mistakes, damage, or danger.
questions.hint: CARE + FUL + LY — double L where "full" meets "ly".
steps: "full" drops one L before -ly: F-U-L, then L-Y.

ex.tip: "Full" has two Ls on its own, but loses one when -ly is added — the other L comes from -ly itself.
